pablo-picasso.example: In Les Demoiselles d’Avignon, Picasso crowds five figures into a shallow space. Three look directly at the viewer. The figures appear from different angles, making it hard to settle on a single viewpoint.
pablo-picasso.locator: Three of the five naked protagonists stare outward

missy-elliott.example: In “Work It,” Elliott puts a backward vocal inside the hook. Listeners can recognize and repeat its sound even before they work out what the reversed phrase says.
At her Rock Hall induction, Elliott linked “Get Ur Freak On,” “Pass That Dutch” and other singles in one live medley. The dancers changed routines as the music moved from one record to the next.
In the video for “The Rain (Supa Dupa Fly),” Elliott raps in an inflated black suit. The changing silhouette gives the beat a visible shape every time she moves.
missy-elliott.locator: inflatable jumpsuit in the music video

david-bowie.example: For his 1973 Ziggy Stardust concert in Dundee, Bowie wore a red jumpsuit designed by Kansai Yamamoto. The costume gave the people at the back of Caird Hall a stage character they could see as well as hear.
The V&A preserves Bowie’s marked-up script for Labyrinth. His notes beside the lines for Jareth give viewers a glimpse of the work behind the performance.
david-bowie.locator: Script with Bowie’s notes for his character Jareth

stevie-wonder.example: As a young Motown musician, Wonder helped write “The Tears of a Clown” for Smokey Robinson. A song associated with another singer’s voice is also a part of Wonder’s career as a writer.

In “Sir Duke,” listen for the short horn phrases and the way the instruments come together for the longer run. The band gives a song celebrating musicianship a passage listeners can recognize without the words.

bob-marley.example: At the 1978 One Love Peace Concert in Kingston, Marley called political rivals Michael Manley and Edward Seaga onstage during “Jamming” and brought their hands together. The audience could see the gesture above the musicians.
bob-marley.locator: One Love Peace Concert in Kingston

bob-marley.example: After tear gas interrupted the 1980 Zimbabwe independence concert, Marley went back onstage to perform “Zimbabwe.” The following evening the Wailers played a free show for the public.
On Uprising, “Redemption Song” pares the arrangement down to Marley’s voice and acoustic guitar. The invitation to sing along is audible without a chorus of backing singers.

fela-kuti.example: “Water No Get Enemy” builds its argument out of an everyday necessity. Fela lets the band establish the groove before he begins listing the things people need water to do.

On “Expensive Shit,” Fela turns a police attempt to catch him with marijuana into an extended comic story. The punch line depends on listeners following the evidence almost as closely as the police do.

billie-jean-king.example: In September 1973, King accepted Bobby Riggs’s challenge and beat him in straight sets at the Houston Astrodome. With a worldwide television audience watching, she took an argument about women’s tennis onto the court.
After winning the 1972 US Open, King said she would sit out the next tournament unless it paid its men’s and women’s champions equally. The 1973 US Open awarded equal prize money.
billie-jean-king.locator: players would pull from the tournament

nadia-comaneci.example: At the 1975 European Championships, Comăneci won the all-around, uneven bars, balance beam and vault. A year before Montreal, she had already given an international audience four different events in which to see her work.
In Montreal in 1976, Comăneci earned Olympic gymnastics’ first perfect ten on the uneven bars. That routine also counted toward Romania’s team competition, where the gymnasts took silver.
nadia-comaneci.locator: first woman to score a perfect 10

nadia-comaneci.example: At the 1980 Moscow Olympics, Comăneci defended her balance beam title and also won gold on floor. Floor gave the audience a different performance from the beam routine for which it already knew her.

katie-ledecky.example: In the 2024 Paris 800-metre final, Ariarne Titmus stayed close enough that Ledecky could never take a comfortable lead. Ledecky led at every turn and finished with a fourth consecutive Olympic title at the distance.
Ledecky won the London Olympic 800 metres in 2012 at fifteen. When she returned to the same event in Paris twelve years later, she was the swimmer a new generation was trying to catch.

jackie-joyner-kersee.example: At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, Joyner-Kersee took silver in the heptathlon. She returned to the same seven-event contest in Seoul four years later and raised the world record to 7,291 points.

Explaining why she started her foundation in 1988, Joyner-Kersee credited people who had helped her grow up in East St. Louis. She described building a community center there so local children could get after-school help.

At the Barcelona Olympics in 1992, Joyner-Kersee defended her heptathlon title and took bronze in the separate long jump. Her jumping counted twice under different rules, once within a seven-event total and once on its own.

When Lehigh asked what she would tell the next generation of leaders, Joyner-Kersee told them to practice active listening and resist pressure to change themselves for acceptance. Her advice extended to how they used social media.

yuna-kim.example: For her Sochi Olympic season, Kim skated her short program to “Send in the Clowns” and her free skate to Astor Piazzolla’s “Adiós Nonino.” The programs, choreographed by David Wilson, gave the same audience two markedly different musical performances.
In Vancouver in 2010, Kim won Olympic gold by combining her short program and free skate across two days. Her free skate earned 150.06 points, bringing her total to 228.56.

tatyana-mcfadden.example: While in high school, McFadden went to court for the chance to race alongside her schoolmates. She later told the International Paralympic Committee that her request was for access to competition and that she had sought no damages.

As a contributor to the documentary Rising Phoenix, McFadden discussed making room for disabled people behind the camera. She drew attention to who made the film as well as to the Paralympians shown on screen.

michael-phelps.example: In Beijing’s 4 × 100-metre freestyle relay, Phelps swam the first leg and then had to watch the finish from the deck. Teammate Jason Lezak caught France’s Alain Bernard on the anchor leg to win for the United States.

At the 2004 Athens Olympics, Phelps swam eight events across individual races and relays. He opened with a world record in the 400-metre individual medley and finished the meet with six golds and two bronzes.

sachin-tendulkar.example: In the 2011 World Cup, Tendulkar contributed more runs across the tournament than any other India batter. The team secured the title in Mumbai against Sri Lanka, with other batters completing the chase.
In Gwalior in 2010, Tendulkar made 200 against South Africa and became the first man to reach a double century in a one-day international. He spent the entire innings at the crease.

tony-hawk.example: At the 1999 X Games, Hawk landed a 900 in front of fellow skaters and spectators after years of trying the two-and-a-half-turn trick. The attempts that preceded the landing were part of what the audience saw.

Hawk’s Boom Boom HuckJam tour brought skateboarders, BMX riders and freestyle motocross riders into a single arena show. Once out of competition, he could put riders from different disciplines on the same bill.
Also in 1999, Hawk worked with Activision on the first Tony Hawk’s Pro Skater. Someone picking up a controller could learn the names of skateboarding tricks before ever stepping onto a ramp.

toni-morrison.example: In The Bluest Eye, Morrison gave Pecola Breedlove a wish for blue eyes. A child’s request made a community’s ideas about beauty visible on the page.
In Beloved, Morrison placed Sethe in a house haunted by the child she lost. The history of slavery enters the novel through what one family must live with at home.
toni-morrison.locator: ghost of her baby, who died nameless

jane-addams.example: Addams campaigned against employing children in industry. The work carried an issue faced by families around Hull-House into a public debate about labor.
At The Hague in 1915, Addams chaired an international women’s peace congress during the First World War. She then urged President Woodrow Wilson to mediate between the countries at war.

selma-lagerlof.example: After traveling in Italy, Lagerlöf set The Miracles of Antichrist in Sicily. The novelist who had introduced readers to Värmland built her next major story around a different landscape.
For Jerusalem, Lagerlöf visited Swedish emigrants in the Holy Land in 1900. She made their decision to leave home the subject of a two-part novel.

Asked to write for elementary pupils, Lagerlöf made The Wonderful Adventures of Nils a journey across Sweden. Children could follow the boy from place to place as they learned the country’s geography.
Lagerlöf entered excerpts from Gösta Berling’s Saga in a Swedish weekly’s competition. Readers met the characters in prizewinning installments before the novel appeared as a book.
selma-lagerlof.locator: first prize in a literary competition

wole-soyinka.example: Soyinka wrote The Lion and the Jewel while working in London, and the comedy was staged in Ibadan. Its journey from manuscript to a Nigerian audience preceded its appearance in print.
In The Bacchae of Euripides, Soyinka adapted a Greek tragedy for a new production. The staging brought his dramatic language into direct conversation with an older theatrical tradition.
For Opera Wonyosi, Soyinka reworked material from John Gay’s The Beggar’s Opera and Bertolt Brecht’s The Threepenny Opera. He brought two earlier satires to bear on the society he was writing about.

marian-anderson.example: In 1939, after she was denied the use of Constitution Hall, Anderson sang outdoors at the Lincoln Memorial. She opened with “America,” giving the audience a melody many could recognize from its first notes.
In 1935, Eleanor Roosevelt invited Anderson to sing at the White House. Her program included spirituals, bringing the songs she knew from church into the presidential residence.
marian-anderson.locator: invited to perform at the White House

john-coltrane.example: Coltrane took “My Favorite Things” from The Sound of Music and played it on soprano saxophone. The familiar waltz melody gives listeners a point of return during an extended improvisation.

In Dizzy Gillespie’s band, Coltrane switched from alto to tenor saxophone at Gillespie’s request. An ensemble’s need changed the instrument through which many listeners first came to recognize his sound.
john-coltrane.locator: switch from alto to tenor saxophone

cathy-freeman.example: At the 1994 Victoria Commonwealth Games she won the 200m and 400m, then carried the Aboriginal and Australian flags together on her victory lap, saying she does not only represent herself but her people.
Before the 1996 Atlanta Olympic 400m final she wrote 48.6 on a piece of paper as the time she needed to beat Marie-Jose Perec, then ran 48.63 and finished second to Perec's Olympic-record 48.25.

After winning the 400m in Sydney in 49.11, she said she was proud to have a place in the history of the country, in a sporting context but also in a social-justice context, for matters important to the future.
cathy-freeman.locator: a place in the history of this country

wilma-rudolph.example: At the 1960 Rome Olympics, Wilma Rudolph won gold in the 100 meters, 200 meters and 4x100-meter relay, becoming the first American woman to win three gold medals in track and field at a single Games.
She retired at twenty-two after winning the 100 meters and anchoring the winning U.S. 4x100-meter relay team at the USA-USSR dual meet at Stanford University.
wilma-rudolph.locator: USSR dual meet at Stanford University

wilma-rudolph.example: Rudolph later worked in youth programs and headed the Wilma Rudolph Foundation, and in 1987 she became head track coach at DePauw University.
wilma-rudolph.locator: became head track coach at DePauw University

florence-griffith-joyner.example: Florence Griffith Joyner's 10.49 in the 100 metres at the 1988 Olympic Trials in Indianapolis is described by USA Track & Field as one of the most eye-popping performances in track and field history.
After transferring from Cal State Northridge to UCLA, she won the NCAA 200 metres championship in 1982 and the 400 metres title in 1983.
florence-griffith-joyner.locator: transferring from Cal State Northridge to UCLA

tanni-grey-thompson.example: Recalling Barcelona 1992, where she won four golds including world records in the 100m and 400m, she said the Games set a standard for others to follow and that it was the first time disability sport got significant media coverage.
In a 2012 Laureus interview, she said it took her a while to find the sport she wanted to concentrate on, and that from the age of thirteen it was wheelchair racing.

Writing for the Telegraph in March 2020, during the postponement of the Tokyo Games, she advised Para athletes to take the positive from the situation, use the time as a training block, and noted that athletes are used to refocusing goals.
tanni-grey-thompson.locator: go back into a training block

kathrine-switzer.example: In 1977 she created the Avon International Running Circuit, a global series of women's races that grew to 400 races in 27 countries for more than a million women; she and the series' participation record are credited as a main factor in getting the women's marathon into the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

After that race she joined with other women in a vocal campaign to make women official competitors in the Boston Marathon, which succeeded in 1972, and later that same year she was one of the creators of the first women's road race.

mia-hamm.example: In 2020 Hamm described joining the investment group behind Angel City, a new women’s professional soccer team in Los Angeles. She was now helping to build a club for the players who would take the field.

On the U.S. Soccer Podcast, Hamm recalled being a supporting player on the 1991 World Cup team. The account gives a younger teammate’s view of a tournament often remembered through its final and its stars.
mia-hamm.locator: role player at the inaugural Women’s World Cup

christine-sinclair.example: At the 2002 FIFA U-19 Women's World Championship in Edmonton, Sinclair won the Golden Boot with 10 goals and the Golden Ball as tournament MVP as Canada finished second.
christine-sinclair.locator: Golden Ball as tournament MVP as Canada

christine-sinclair.example: At London 2012, she was the tournament's leading scorer with six of Canada's 12 goals, including a hat trick in the semifinal against the United States, and was named Canada's Closing Ceremony flag bearer.
In June 2021, her hometown of Burnaby, British Columbia announced it would rename the local sport and health facility the Christine Sinclair Community Centre.

gertrude-ederle.example: At the 1924 Paris Olympics she won gold and a world record as the leadoff swimmer on the 400-meter freestyle relay, and took bronze in the 100-meter and 400-meter freestyle races, per the International Swimming Hall of Fame.

Her first Channel attempt, on August 18, 1925, ended when her coach Jabez Wolffe, concerned for her safety, ordered support-crew member Ishak Helmy to pull her from the water; the Hall of Fame's centennial account records that Ederle vehemently disagreed with the decision. She returned in 1926 with different sponsors and a different coach and crew.

On August 6, 1926, Ederle crossed the Channel from France to England in 14 hours 39 minutes, beating the previous speed record of 16 hours 33 minutes, according to the Hall of Fame's centennial account, which also notes she wore a two-piece bathing suit and personally designed wrap-around goggles kept watertight with molten candle wax.

fanny-blankers-koen.example: From a 1936 Olympic debut in which she finished fifth in the high jump and 4x100m relay, she went on to serve as Dutch athletics team manager from the 1958 European Championships to the Mexico City 1968 Olympic Games, and the Netherlands' prominent FBK Games in Hengelo, an annual fixture since 1981, is named after her and held in a stadium that also bears her name.
fanny-blankers-koen.locator: Dutch athletics team manager from the 1958

fanny-blankers-koen.example: Before the 1952 Helsinki Olympics she ran her fastest-ever times for 100 yards, 100m and 200m, but, suffering from a painful carbuncle on her leg, she withdrew from the 100m semi-finals to save her strength for the 80m hurdles final, then pulled up in that final after hitting the first two hurdles hard. She was still top of the world lists for the 80m hurdles in 1953 with 11.1.

novak-djokovic.example: In the 2023 Cincinnati final he saved a championship point to beat Carlos Alcaraz in what the ATP Tour calls one of the greatest three-set finals and the longest best-of-three final in ATP Tour history since 1990.
At the 2024 Paris Olympics he won his first Olympic gold medal without dropping a set, after beating Rafael Nadal in the second round.

arthur-ashe.example: In 1969 he co-founded the National Junior Tennis League with Charlie Pasarell and Sheridan Snyder, a program built to bring tennis to children who might not otherwise get to play and to pair the sport with discipline and attention to academics; Ashe framed the effort as using tennis to teach life skills rather than to produce professional athletes.
arthur-ashe.locator: National Junior Tennis League with Charlie Pasarell

arthur-ashe.example: Ashe began applying for a South African visa in 1969 to enter the South African Open and was refused despite holding the No. 1 U.S. ranking, and he kept applying through repeated denials while campaigning for the country's expulsion from the International Lawn Tennis Federation.

haile-gebrselassie.example: Running in Zurich in 1995, he took nearly 11 seconds off Moses Kiptanui's 5000m world record with a time of 12:44.39, a race he later named as his finest performance.
At the 1993 IAAF World Championships in Stuttgart, Gebrselassie won the 10,000m title, the first of four successive world 10,000m crowns he would collect through 1999.

carl-lewis.example: At the 1984 Los Angeles Games, Carl Lewis won the 100m, 200m, long jump and 4x100m relay, matching Jesse Owens's 1936 feat in the same four events.

At the 1991 World Championships in Tokyo, Lewis broke the 100m world record with 9.86 while winning the event; at the same meet, his long-jump streak of 65 consecutive victories ended against Mike Powell.
At the 1992 Olympics, Lewis won the long jump and ran the anchor leg on the U.S. 4x100m relay, which set a world record of 37.40.
carl-lewis.locator: anchoring the U.S. team to a world record

lewis-hamilton.example: At the 2008 British Grand Prix, Hamilton started from fourth, took two positions on the opening lap and then took the lead from McLaren team mate Heikki Kovalainen a few laps later, going on to win by 68.577 seconds in increasingly heavy rain — a drive Formula 1 has described as one of the greatest performances in the sport.
lewis-hamilton.locator: lead from McLaren team mate Heikki Kovalainen

lewis-hamilton.example: Entering the 2008 finale in Brazil seven points ahead of Felipe Massa, Hamilton needed fifth place to secure his first title; Massa won the race, and Hamilton climbed to fifth on the final lap to take the championship by a single point.

After his emotional 2024 victory at Silverstone, Hamilton brought his loved ones onto the fan stage with him to celebrate — a gesture Formula 1 noted alongside his long habit of paying tribute to his family's support.

ayrton-senna.example: Midway through the 1988 season, in his first year as Alain Prost's McLaren teammate, Senna was asked at a press conference whether it was possible for the two to be equal; he answered that there could only be one winner, a reply Formula 1's retrospective records.
At the 1985 Portuguese Grand Prix, Senna took the first pole position and first win of his Formula 1 career, race day run in wet conditions, as Formula 1's profile records.

During his 1984 rookie season with Toleman, Senna opened talks with Lotus in the background, which Formula 1's profile describes as a breach of his Toleman contract, and he was suspended for a race late that year.

jackie-robinson.example: In October 1945, Brooklyn Dodgers general manager Branch Rickey announced he had signed Robinson; Robinson played the 1946 season with the Triple-A Montreal Royals of the International League, then became the first Black player to appear in a modern big league game with Brooklyn on April 15, 1947.
jackie-robinson.locator: Brooklyn Dodgers general manager Branch Rickey announced

jackie-robinson.example: Robinson won the NCAA long jump title with a leap of 24 feet, 10½ inches, the Hall of Fame records, after playing for the 1939 UCLA Bruins football team.

At Game 2 of the 1972 World Series, nine days before his death on October 24, Robinson made his final public appearance and voiced his hope that a Major League Baseball team would soon hire the game's first Black manager.
jackie-robinson.locator: voiced his hope that a Major League

magic-johnson.example: In Game 6 of the 1980 NBA Finals at Philadelphia on May 16, with Kareem Abdul-Jabbar out injured, Johnson scored 42 points, grabbed 15 rebounds and handed out seven assists as the Lakers clinched the title, and he became the first—and still only—rookie to win Finals MVP.
On April 15, 1991, against Dallas, Johnson recorded his 9,888th career assist on a pass to Terry Teagle, overtaking Oscar Robertson's 17-year-old mark to become the NBA's all-time assist leader.

On Nov. 7, 1991, Johnson announced that he had tested positive for HIV and was retiring from the NBA; he returned at the 1992 All-Star Game, where he scored 25 points with nine assists and was named All-Star Game MVP.
After the 1991 announcement he became a prominent spokesman for HIV/AIDS awareness, and two years later he rejoined the Lakers as interim coach near the end of the 1993-94 season, NBA.com records.

kareem-abdul-jabbar.example: In the 1971 NBA Finals, Abdul-Jabbar and Oscar Robertson helped Milwaukee beat Baltimore in four straight games. It was the first NBA title for both teammates.
In the 1985 Finals, Abdul-Jabbar helped the Lakers recover from a heavy opening loss to beat Boston. At thirty-eight he was named the series’ most valuable player.

dan-carter.example: In Wellington in 2005, Carter scored 33 points against the British and Irish Lions. New Zealand took the second Test and secured the series.
In Rome in 2004, Carter started at first five-eighth for the All Blacks against Italy. The No. 10 position made him the link between the forwards and the backs.
dan-carter.locator: Carter took hold of the 10 jersey

dan-carter.example: When he accepted the players’ union’s Special Merit Award in 2025, Carter described the DC10 Fund’s work with UNICEF for children in the Pacific. He used the presentation to name a project people could support.
dan-carter.locator: the work I do for DC10 fund

dan-carter.example: At the launch of the Global Rugby Players Foundation, Carter set out its purpose of helping professional players move into life after rugby. His appeal included players from women’s and men’s teams in both the fifteen-a-side and sevens games.

edwin-moses.example: At the 1976 Montreal Olympics, in his first year running the 400 metres hurdles, Edwin Moses won gold in a world record 47.64 seconds, per Laureus.

Laureus records that in 2000 his fellow academy members elected him unanimously as the inaugural Chairman of the Laureus World Sports Academy, and that he stood down in 2016, by which time Laureus supported more than 100 projects worldwide.
edwin-moses.locator: inaugural Chairman of the Laureus World Sports

edwin-moses.example: In 1983 in Koblenz he set a world record of 47.02 seconds, his fourth, a mark Laureus says stood unchallenged for nine years. In 2012 he was named in the inaugural IAAF Hall of Fame, one of 13 athletes in that first group.
edwin-moses.locator: in Koblenz, with a time of 47.02

yuzuru-hanyu.example: The ISU records that Hanyu performed the first clean quadruple loop in competition at the 2016 Autumn Classic in Canada, a scored event on the calendar rather than an exhibition.
According to the ISU, Hanyu became the first skater to surpass a total score of 300 points, reaching 322.40 at NHK Trophy in 2015.

rachel-carson.example: The Sea Around Us brought ocean science to a broad readership in 1951. Carson moved from the history of ocean basins to currents and tides readers might recognize close to home.
For Under the Sea-Wind, Carson followed the lives of marine animals. She invited readers into ocean ecology through the movements of creatures such as a shorebird and a migrating eel.

jane-goodall.example: In 1986 Goodall helped organize the Understanding Chimpanzees conference in Chicago. Hearing researchers describe disappearing habitat helped move conservation to the center of her public work.
In 1991 Tanzanian students asked Goodall what young people could do for their communities. Their conversation developed into Roots & Shoots, a program built around locally chosen projects.
jane-goodall.locator: students in Tanzania reach out to Jane

katherine-johnson.example: With engineer Ted Skopinski, Johnson published a 1960 report on the direction a spacecraft would need to take to pass over a chosen point. Her name appeared alongside his on the research.
Before his orbital flight in 1962, John Glenn asked Johnson to check the electronic computer’s numbers. She worked through the trajectory herself before the mission went ahead.
On Apollo, Johnson worked on the calculations that brought the lunar module and the orbiting command module back together. The two spacecraft’s separate journeys had to meet at one place and time.

chien-shiung-wu.example: In 1975 Wu became the first woman to serve as president of the American Physical Society. The office put a working experimentalist who had publicly challenged sex discrimination at the head of her professional association.
chien-shiung-wu.locator: president of the American Physical Society

chien-shiung-wu.example: At MIT in 1964, Wu asked a scientific audience why the sex of the person doing a calculation should matter to the physical world being described. She used their own discipline to challenge unequal treatment in it.

dorothy-hodgkin.example: During the Second World War, Hodgkin and her colleagues determined the structure of penicillin. Their interpretation settled a disagreement about the shape of a medically important molecule.

As president of the Pugwash Conferences, Hodgkin worked with scientists across Cold War divisions on disarmament. The forum let people from opposing political systems meet around a shared public question.

Hodgkin’s team mapped the much larger vitamin B12 molecule. Working through its elaborate structure showed what crystallography could establish about compounds too complicated to picture by inspection.
After decades of work, Hodgkin and her colleagues reported the structure of insulin in 1969. The published model marked a result she had begun pursuing early in her career.

bertha-von-suttner.example: In Lay Down Your Arms!, von Suttner followed a woman whose family is repeatedly struck by war. The novel gave readers the costs of military conflict from inside a household.
In letters to Alfred Nobel, von Suttner argued for support for organized peace work. The two kept up their exchange well after the brief period she had worked for him.
bertha-von-suttner.locator: corresponded for years on the subject of peace

leymah-gbowee.example: Gbowee helped organize Liberian Christian and Muslim women in a joint peace movement. They wore white and gathered publicly, making a coalition across religious lines visible.
The women pressed President Charles Taylor to attend peace talks. Gbowee helped deliver a specific request to the person whose participation they sought.
When the Accra talks stalled in 2003, Gbowee and other activists held a sit-in at the meeting site. They brought the consequences of delay into the negotiators’ immediate surroundings.

alexander-von-humboldt.example: For his chart of New Spain, Humboldt brought geographic information about a vast territory into a single map. Copies circulated beyond the people who had participated in the original survey work.

In his plant-geography diagram of Chimborazo, Humboldt put plants at different elevations on the same mountain outline. A reader could see relationships among altitude, climate and vegetation at a glance.

c-v-raman.example: Raman founded the Indian Journal of Physics in 1926. Editing the journal created a route for researchers to put their findings into circulation from India.
c-v-raman.locator: founded the Indian Journal of Physics

c-v-raman.example: Raman published studies of how instruments in the violin family produce sound. Music that listeners could recognize became a problem he could debate with other physicists in print.
c-v-raman.locator: musical instruments of the violin family

kofi-annan.example: Annan proposed the Global Compact to business leaders at Davos. He asked companies to make public commitments on labor, human rights and environmental principles.
In his 2000 Millennium Report, Annan set out priorities for heads of state meeting at the United Nations. The proposals helped shape the Millennium Declaration and its shared development commitments.
In 2001 Annan called for a global fund to confront HIV/AIDS and other major diseases. He put a specific financing proposal before governments as part of the international response.

janet-jagan.example: Jagan helped found the Union of Guyanese Journalists with fellow journalists Clinton Collymore, Moses Nagamotoo and Kellawan Lall, and became its first President.
Jagan became Minister of Home Affairs in 1963 on the death of Claude Christian and was appointed to the Senate; in 1964 she resigned as Minister in protest over incidents in Wismar.
janet-jagan.locator: Minister in protest over incidents in Wismar

hiram-rhodes-revels.example: In his final Senate speech, Hiram Revels defended legislation to prohibit discrimination in District of Columbia schools based on race, color, or previous condition of servitude.
hiram-rhodes-revels.locator: prohibit discrimination in District of Columbia schools

hiram-rhodes-revels.example: Hiram Revels became the first president of Alcorn University in Mississippi, the institution named for his political ally Governor James Alcorn; after the election of Governor Adelbert Ames in 1874, Revels resigned the Alcorn presidency.
On March 16, 1870, Hiram Revels delivered his maiden Senate speech, defending the Black legislators expelled from Georgia's legislature and urging Congress to restore their seats.
hiram-rhodes-revels.locator: defended the Black legislators in Georgia

clara-campoamor.example: As a deputy, Clara Campoamor debated the organizing principles of the Tribunal Tutelar de Menores, Spain's juvenile guardianship court, taking part in parliamentary discussion of how the child-protection body should be structured.

As a deputy, Campoamor presented her own divorce bill, then withdrew it to support the government's version, approved in 1932. She also pressed for abolition of regulated prostitution, investigation of paternity and legitimacy for children born outside marriage.
clara-campoamor.locator: Presentó su propia ley del divorcio

charles-de-gaulle.example: Having left government and stayed silent for months, de Gaulle travelled to Bayeux on 16 June 1946 to present his constitutional plan: a strong executive with the head of state as its cornerstone, alongside a bicameral parliament.
From London, de Gaulle asked Churchill for permission to speak on the BBC and on 18 June urged French officers, soldiers, engineers and armament workers in Britain to contact him and keep fighting.
charles-de-gaulle.locator: officers and soldiers who were on British territory

tomas-garrigue-masaryk.example: During his wartime negotiations in the United States, Masaryk signed the Pittsburgh Agreement, a 1918 memorandum between Czech and Slovak expatriate organizations on their intent to create a common independent state.

After returning to Prague in December 1918, Masaryk delivered his first declaration to the National Assembly at the Castle the following day. He opened it with a quotation from Comenius's Testament addressed to the Czech people.
tomas-garrigue-masaryk.locator: first declaration to the National Assembly

adolfo-suarez.example: In April 1977 Suárez's government legalised the Communist Party of Spain, a decision that stirred the more conservative Francoist sectors but cleared a central obstacle to democratic elections that June.
Weakened in parliament and within his own party, Suárez offered his resignation on 29 January 1981 as head of government and as UCD president, and Leopoldo Calvo-Sotelo replaced him in both posts.

sarojini-naidu.example: In 1908 Sarojini Naidu spoke at the Indian National Social Conference in Madras, advocating reforms to improve conditions of widows.
sarojini-naidu.locator: Indian National Social Conference in Madras

sarojini-naidu.example: In 1917 Sarojini Naidu headed the All-India Women's Deputation and championed women's suffrage before E. S. Montagu, Secretary of State for India.

aung-san-suu-kyi.example: In September 1988 Aung San Suu Kyi helped establish the National League for Democracy. Despite a ban on meetings, she took its political case to public gatherings around the country.

In an open letter in 1988, Aung San Suu Kyi urged Burma’s government to bring independent figures into a committee that could oversee a transition to multiparty elections. She also pressed for the release of political prisoners.
aung-san-suu-kyi.locator: consultative committee of respected independent persons

takako-doi.example: In Japan’s 2005 general election, former Social Democratic Party leader Takako Doi took the last place on the party’s five-candidate Kinki proportional representation list. Its one seat went to Kiyomi Tsujimoto, who was first on the list.
takako-doi.locator: Tsujimoto, who was placed at the top

takako-doi.example: After losing her seat in the September 2005 election, Doi told a news conference in Hyogo Prefecture that she would continue to defend the Constitution. She had resigned as party leader after the earlier 2003 election.
takako-doi.locator: a news conference held in Hyogo Prefecture

rawya-ateya.example: In her memoir, Ateya said she trained women in first aid and nursing during the 1956 Suez crisis. Teaching those skills gave other volunteers a way to take part in the relief effort.

Recalling a July 1957 campaign meeting, Ateya said she asked why she alone should withdraw when seven candidates were running. She declined the offer to reimburse her campaign expenses and stayed in the race.

In the National Assembly, Ateya asked the minister of social affairs and labor to implement a plan for family guidance and marriage counseling offices. She identified a service that families could use and the minister responsible for putting it into practice.
During the October War of 1973, Ateya chaired the Society of Families of Martyrs and Soldiers. The people her organization served included military families and those who had lost someone in service.

sheikh-mujibur-rahman.example: On 24 or 25 December 1962, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman requested a meeting with Indian official Sashanka S Banerjee and handed him a letter dated 25 December 1962 addressed to Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru seeking India's support for his liberation struggle.

In January 1972, after release from Mianwali Prison, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman flew from Rawalpindi via London and Delhi toward Dhaka, and the Indian diplomat accompanying him did so under a brief from Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

jose-ramos-horta.example: Ramos-Horta left East Timor in 1975 to serve as foreign minister for the FRETILIN liberation movement, then spent roughly two decades traveling worldwide to argue the East Timorese cause before the United Nations and other audiences.

In 1992 Ramos-Horta put forward a peace plan to advance dialogue with Indonesia, proposing humanitarian cooperation with the occupying power and a larger UN-led international presence meant to prepare for withdrawal and self-determination.

kwame-nkrumah.example: Kwame Nkrumah, then a student in London, attended the Fifth Pan-African Congress in Manchester in 1945, where delegates demanded an immediate end to colonialism and asserted Africans' right to self-government.

In his Independence Day speech on 6 March 1957, Nkrumah pledged that Ghana's freedom would be tied to the liberation of the rest of Africa, committing the new nation to assist anti-colonial movements.

ahmed-kathrada.example: Kathrada distributed Young Communist League leaflets at street corners after joining in 1941, an early activist task he chose for himself rather than a formal office.
In 1951 Kathrada attended the World Youth Festival in Berlin as chairperson of the Transvaal Indian Youth Congress and was elected leader of the multi-racial South African delegation.
ahmed-kathrada.locator: attended the World Youth Festival in Berlin

kader-asmal.example: Asmal chaired the World Commission on Dams, which reported in December 2000 after an independent global review of the costs and benefits of large dam projects.
Asmal was chairperson of the Irish Anti-Apartheid Movement from 1972 until 1991, organising opposition to apartheid from his base in Dublin.

kofi-abrefa-busia.example: Busia's 1951 Oxford University Press monograph examined how contemporary social change reshaped Ashanti political institutions, treating chiefs' authority as a subject for documented fieldwork rather than assumption.
Busia recorded a radio and television broadcast on 20 April 1970 arguing for fair trial for all in Ghana, addressing the public directly through state broadcasting.
kofi-abrefa-busia.locator: radio and television broadcast on Monday

dolly-parton.example: In “Coat of Many Colors,” Parton remembers her mother sewing a coat from scraps and her classmates laughing at it. The garment stays the same while its meaning changes from home to school.

In “Jolene,” Parton has the narrator address the woman she fears losing her partner to. In an NPR interview about the song, Parton traced that character’s name to a young fan. A stranger’s name became the person a listener hears the narrator pleading with.
dolly-parton.locator: vulnerability of the woman pleading with Jolene

yayoi-kusama.example: In Infinity Mirror Room—Phalli’s Field, red-spotted fabric forms cover the floor. Mirrors repeat them so thoroughly that it becomes hard to tell where the sewn objects end.
In All the Eternal Love I Have for the Pumpkins, glowing, spotted pumpkins repeat in mirrored walls. Walking beside them lets a visitor see a modest patch turn into a field with no visible edge.

allyson-felix.example: At the London Olympics in 2012, Felix ran on both winning U.S. relay teams as well as winning the individual 200 metres. Her teammates counted on her across two different relay distances at the same meet.
In Beijing in 2015, Felix won the world 400-metre title. Her earlier global titles had come over 200 metres, and this time she had to sustain her race for a full lap.
In Tokyo, Felix followed her individual 400-metre bronze with a final Olympic relay. She earned gold alongside her U.S. teammates in the 4 × 400 metres, sharing the last podium of her Olympic career.

shingo-kunieda.example: In the 2022 Wimbledon final, Kunieda came through a deciding set against Alfie Hewett to claim the singles title missing from his collection. The venue was familiar from his earlier wheelchair doubles championships.

For his last career singles title, Kunieda faced sixteen-year-old Tokito Oda at the 2022 Japan Open. Seven thousand spectators watched the veteran and teenager take their final set to a tiebreak at Tokyo’s Ariake Tennis Park.

marie-curie.example: When pitchblende proved more radioactive than its uranium could explain, Marie and Pierre Curie reported what they thought was missing. In 1898 they announced polonium and then, with Gustave Bémont, radium.
marie-curie.locator: pitchblende contains at least two radioactive materials

marie-curie.example: In her 1911 Nobel lecture, Curie named André-Louis Debierne as her collaborator on obtaining metallic radium. She distinguished that 1910 result from the earlier discovery of the element.

tu-youyou.example: When Tu took charge of her institute’s malaria project in 1969, she and her colleagues searched medical texts and consulted practitioners. They gathered promising accounts into a collection for the research effort.
tu-youyou.locator: head and build a Project 523 research group

tu-youyou.example: At a national project meeting in Nanjing in 1972, Tu reported her team’s results on qinghao. Other groups could compare them with the leads they were pursuing.

elinor-ostrom.example: In studies of American metropolitan policing, Ostrom and her colleagues compared which services small and large departments could deliver. They examined individual tasks before judging the size of a whole organization.
elinor-ostrom.locator: polycentric police industries serving US metropolitan areas

elinor-ostrom.example: In Nepal, Ostrom’s team compared irrigation systems managed by farmers with systems managed by government agencies. Their comparison gave farmers’ working rules a place alongside the physical condition of the canals.
elinor-ostrom.locator: grow more rice, distribute water more equitably

elinor-ostrom.example: In experiments on shared resources, Ostrom and her collaborators let some participants talk face to face. They could then compare what people actually took when conversation was possible with what happened when it was barred.
elinor-ostrom.locator: a series of face-to-face communication experiments

amartya-sen.example: In Poverty and Famines, Sen asked how people could starve even when enough food existed. He followed what workers could buy with their wages, moving the argument from grain totals to families’ access to food.

In his work on social choice, Sen showed how a collective rule can run up against the liberty of individuals to decide matters for themselves. He made the conflict precise enough for others to challenge his assumptions.
When developing a poverty index, Sen included the distribution of income among poor people. A transfer between two people below the poverty line could then change what the measure reported.

muhammad-yunus.example: In the village of Jobra, Yunus and his students made a list of people whose debts tied them to moneylenders. He covered the small total himself and then asked a local bank to lend to the villagers.
In his Nobel lecture, Yunus argued that lasting peace requires reducing poverty. He asked governments to examine how spending priorities reflected their understanding of security.
muhammad-yunus.locator: peace is inextricably linked to poverty

john-steinbeck.example: For The Harvest Gypsies, Steinbeck reported on migrant agricultural workers in California. Newspaper readers encountered the living conditions in the camps before he returned to the subject in fiction.

The Log from the Sea of Cortez recounts a collecting expedition Steinbeck made with marine biologist Ed Ricketts. He placed the work of observing animals alongside conversations about how people see the natural world.

rabindranath-tagore.example: For the English Gitanjali, Tagore translated a selection of his own Bengali poems, drawing from several collections. He shaped a new sequence for readers encountering the poems in English.
In The Gardener, Tagore gathered English versions of poems from his Bengali writing. Choosing which pieces belonged together was part of how he introduced this work to a new readership.

abdulrazak-gurnah.example: In Paradise, Gurnah recast the story of Joseph around Yusuf’s journey in colonial East Africa. Readers familiar with the earlier story encounter a young man facing a very different choice at the end.
abdulrazak-gurnah.locator: retelling of the Quran’s story of Joseph

abdulrazak-gurnah.example: In Admiring Silence, Gurnah’s narrator invents a past for the English family he lives among. Readers have to follow both what he chooses to tell them and what maintaining that story costs him.
abdulrazak-gurnah.locator: hide his past from his English family

joan-baez.example: On her Southern college tours, Baez required that audiences be integrated. That decision made the terms for putting on a concert part of what the concert communicated.
joan-baez.locator: she refused to play at segregated college venues

joan-baez.example: Baez declined to appear on television’s Hootenanny after the program excluded Pete Seeger. Her absence made a position public without a performance on the show.
joan-baez.locator: refused to appear on the show because of Seeger’s listing

deng-yaping.example: At the 1992 Barcelona Olympics, Deng Yaping and Qiao Hong beat Chen Zihe and Gao Jun three sets to one in the women's doubles final; in the singles final Deng then faced Qiao Hong as an opponent and won by the same score, 3-1.
deng-yaping.locator: Chen Zihe and Gao Jun, winning

deng-yaping.example: In the 1996 Atlanta doubles quarter-final, Deng Yaping and Qiao Hong were taken to a fifth set by Chinese Taipei's Jin Chen and Chiutan Chen and won it by a two-point margin.
deng-yaping.locator: the last set with only a two-point lead

deng-yaping.example: Two days after that quarter-final, Deng Yaping met Jin Chen again in the Atlanta singles final: she won the first two games, Chen levelled at two-all, and Deng opened the deciding set with nine points in a row, closing it 21-5.

birgit-fischer.example: After taking gold in the K2 and K4 500m and silver in the K1 500m at Seoul 1988, she took a three-year break following the birth of her second child and returned in time to prepare for Barcelona 1992.

From 1992 until her second retirement she trained without a coach or group, explaining that it was important for her to be able to allocate her time and rank her strengths correctly, and she later said with a smile that alongside the medals she raised two children and earned two degrees.

diana-taurasi.example: On June 18, 2017, at Los Angeles, her basket with 45.3 seconds left in the second quarter moved her past Tina Thompson as the WNBA’s all-time leading scorer, in her 377th career game.
On August 3, 2023, against Atlanta, Taurasi scored her 10,000th WNBA point. She became the first player in league history to reach that total.
diana-taurasi.locator: First player in league history to score 10,000 points

grace-hopper.example: With FLOW-MATIC, Hopper and her team showed how business programs could be expressed in English-like commands. The language later influenced the design of COBOL.
In her Navy work, Hopper pressed for common standards for programming languages. The question was whether software written for one manufacturer’s machine could be understood on another.

florence-nightingale.example: During the Crimean War, Nightingale led nurses to military hospitals at Scutari. The work put her in a position to report directly on the conditions wounded soldiers faced.
The nursing school established with the Nightingale Fund at St Thomas’ Hospital opened in 1860. It gave nurses a place to train and carried her reforms into other hospitals through their work.
florence-nightingale.locator: Nightingale Training School at St Thomas’ Hospital

rosalind-franklin.example: During the Second World War, Franklin investigated the structure of coal and charcoal. Her publications explained why different coals behave differently when heated.
rosalind-franklin.locator: studied coal for her PhD during the war

rosalind-franklin.example: At Birkbeck, Franklin led a group studying the structure of viruses. Their published work on tobacco mosaic virus extended the use of diffraction images to a new biological question.

vera-rubin.example: For her master’s research, Rubin investigated whether the motions of galaxies showed a large-scale pattern. She presented the result at an American Astronomical Society meeting while still at the beginning of her career.
vera-rubin.locator: masters thesis on large-scale motion of galaxies

vera-rubin.example: Rubin and her collaborators extended their observations beyond Andromeda to other spiral galaxies. Showing that the pattern recurred made it harder to dismiss as a peculiarity of one galaxy.
vera-rubin.locator: collected data on dozens of galaxies

mary-anning.example: After her brother Joseph found an ichthyosaur skull near Lyme Regis, Anning excavated the rest of the skeleton. The assembled animal gave researchers more to compare than an isolated fossil bone.
mary-anning.locator: older brother Joseph discovered an enormous

mary-anning.example: In 1823 Anning unearthed a nearly complete plesiosaur. Its unusually long neck could be studied from an articulated skeleton instead of reconstructed from scattered fragments.
mary-anning.locator: first complete, articulated skeleton of a plesiosaur

mary-anning.example: Anning also recovered a pterosaur from the cliffs at Lyme Regis. It supplied evidence of a winged reptile in Britain, far from the German localities then known for such finds.
mary-anning.locator: a flying reptile known as a pterosaur

frederick-douglass.example: In his 1845 Narrative, Douglass recounted learning to read while enslaved and the efforts made to prevent it. A personal history placed before readers became an argument about who controlled access to knowledge.
frederick-douglass.locator: presenting a stark picture of his early life

frederick-douglass.example: In Rochester, Douglass founded The North Star, an antislavery newspaper. Editing it gave him a way to address readers regularly and publish voices alongside his own.
frederick-douglass.locator: First issue of The North Star

alan-turing.example: In 1936 Turing described an imagined machine that follows a finite set of instructions. That simple model let mathematicians ask which problems could, even in principle, be computed.

In The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis, Turing used mathematics to investigate how patterns might emerge in living tissue. The paper carried a question about biological form into a field able to model it.

nikola-tesla.example: In an 1888 lecture to the American Institute of Electrical Engineers, Tesla presented his work on alternating-current motors and transformers. He put the proposed system before the engineers who might evaluate and use it.
nikola-tesla.locator: A new system of alternate current motors

nikola-tesla.example: In his lectures on high-frequency currents, Tesla made lamps glow in front of audiences. The demonstrations turned unfamiliar electrical effects into something spectators could see.

desmond-tutu.example: As chair of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Tutu listened to public testimony about abuses committed under apartheid. The hearings made space for people whose experiences had rarely entered an official record.
Tutu became the first chair of The Elders, bringing former leaders together to work on conflicts and human rights. The role required a group of prominent individuals to speak and act together.
desmond-tutu.locator: Founding member and Chair of The Elders

therese-casgrain.example: In 1938, as vice-president of the Montreal Liberal Women's Club, Casgrain helped secure an invitation for a delegation of about 40 women to the provincial Liberal convention and won support for the Club's proposal to add women's provincial suffrage to the Quebec Liberal platform.
Casgrain hosted Fémina, a bilingual radio program, from 1935 to 1943, using it to raise public awareness of current affairs and women's rights.
Casgrain became president of Quebec’s provincial suffrage committee in 1928. As it reorganized into the Ligue des droits de la femme, membership under her leadership grew to more than 400.
therese-casgrain.locator: la Ligue comptera plus de 400 membres

jeanne-sauve.example: In her installation speech as governor general, Sauvé spoke about the need for Canadians to forego a narrow sense of their nation and become more tolerant.
jeanne-sauve.locator: forego a narrow sense of their nation

jeanne-sauve.example: During her mandate as governor general, Jeanne Sauvé established two awards at Rideau Hall for students wishing to enter the field of special education for exceptional children.

bertha-lutz.example: In 1945 Bertha Lutz headed the Brazilian delegation to the San Francisco Conference and pressed for the equality of men and women, which was recognized in the preamble and in article 8 of the Charter of the United Nations.
bertha-lutz.locator: defendeu a igualdade entre homens e mulheres

bertha-lutz.example: In 1919 Bertha Lutz founded the League for the Intellectual Emancipation of Women, which was the forerunner of the Brazilian Federation for the Progress of Women (FBPF), and she campaigned for the women's vote.
bertha-lutz.locator: Liga para a Emancipação Intelectual da Mulher

matilde-hidalgo.example: In June 1924 Hidalgo asked an electoral board to register her; refused, she petitioned Ecuador's Council of State, which on 9 June 1924, after reviewing the 1906 Constitution, authorized her to cast her vote in those elections.
matilde-hidalgo.locator: junta electoral para solicitar su empadronamiento

matilde-hidalgo.example: In 1930, voters elected Hidalgo and Bertha Valverde to Machala’s municipal council. Hidalgo later became the council’s first woman vice president, giving her a role in running the institution as well as a seat in it.

jose-figueres-ferrer.example: In 1948, as head of the Founding Junta of the Second Republic, José Figueres Ferrer publicly announced two measures the Junta had taken—the nationalization of banking and a 10% capital levy—which were promulgated as a decree days later.
jose-figueres-ferrer.locator: la nacionalización bancaria y el impuesto del 10% sobre el capital

jose-figueres-ferrer.example: In 1948, the Founding Junta of the Second Republic was established by a solemn oath to restore constitutional life, and José Figueres Ferrer was named its president.
jose-figueres-ferrer.locator: Actuará como Presidente de la Junta

ulysses-guimaraes.example: In 1984, Ulysses Guimarães took part in Diretas Já rallies, including a demonstration in Salvador on January 20 alongside Tancredo Neves and Caetano Veloso, as one of the leading figures in the campaign for direct presidential elections.
ulysses-guimaraes.locator: Comício com a presença do deputado ULYSSES GUIMARÃES

ulysses-guimaraes.example: As national president of the MDB and a federal deputy, Ulysses Guimarães in 1979 called the government's amnesty bill restrictive and announced that the opposition would present an amendment to remove that character, honoring the party's commitment to a broad, general and unrestricted amnesty.

nancy-astor.example: Astor supported the provision of nursery schools as part of a broader Commons campaign on women's issues, alongside widows' pensions, more women police and improved maternity services, pressing these causes in debate during the interwar years.

Nancy Astor backed recruiting more women police as part of a broader programme of women's causes. A profile of her parliamentary career lists that campaign alongside nursery schools, widows' pensions and improved maternity services among the efforts she supported.

betty-boothroyd.example: When Betty Boothroyd became Speaker in 1992, she introduced her own personal warm style to the high office, designing a suitable outfit and dispensing with the traditional wig, an observable break from the office's visible conventions.

Under Tony Blair's government, Speaker Betty Boothroyd cautioned politicians favouring family-friendly sitting hours against neglecting the formal scrutiny role the Commons offers, defending the chamber's examination of legislation.
betty-boothroyd.locator: formal scrutiny role offered by the Commons

harriet-harman.example: Harriet Harman piloted the Equality Act 2010 through Parliament, consolidating and improving existing anti-discrimination laws. The Act replaced various earlier statutes, including the Equal Pay Act 1970.
Harman was the prime mover behind Labour's 1993 decision to introduce women-only shortlists in half of all target seats; the policy is credited as a major factor in electing 101 Labour women in 1997.

mary-lou-mcdonald.example: In a Dáil speech marking 25 years since the Good Friday Agreement referendum, Mary Lou McDonald asked the Taoiseach to press for an early British-Irish Intergovernmental Conference at Taoiseach and Prime Minister level to restore the Northern Ireland Executive.
mary-lou-mcdonald.locator: early meeting of the British-Irish Intergovernmental Conference

mary-lou-mcdonald.example: In a May 2023 Dáil exchange about energy bills, McDonald contrasted falling wholesale electricity costs with rising household bills. She used the gap between the two figures to challenge whether savings were reaching consumers.

edith-cresson.example: From 1987 to 1991, Édith Cresson served as president of France Exporte Plus, an association created to help small and medium-sized French businesses enter foreign markets. The role paralleled her parliamentary mandate for Vienne.
edith-cresson.locator: President of the France Exporte Plus association

edith-cresson.example: As Minister for European Affairs in Michel Rocard's government from 1988 to 1990, Cresson formed the Groupes d'Études et de Mobilisation, drawing experts into work on major European issues including the Schengen Agreements, the European automotive industry and public audiovisual services.
edith-cresson.locator: She formed the Groupes d’Études et de Mobilisation

johanna-sigurdardottir.example: During her years as an opposition MP, Jóhanna Sigurðardóttir proposed a bill calling for a constitutional assembly, and she brought such a bill forward again in 1998, after years of arguing that the Constitution needed revision.

Having proposed constitutional-assembly bills twice, in 1994 and 1998, Sigurðardóttir led a minority government whose supporting party made calling a constitutional assembly a condition of its backing, putting the proposal on the agenda.
johanna-sigurdardottir.locator: the condition that the new minority government

kersti-kaljulaid.example: At a UN Security Council meeting on climate and security, Kersti Kaljulaid set out four points, urging the same collective urgency against climate change shown during the pandemic: vaccine-speed solutions, fairer cost-sharing and a scientific data-based approach.

At the Security Council, Kaljulaid invited countries to join Estonia’s Data for the Environment Alliance. She linked the invitation to a concrete offer: working with the UN Environment Programme on a shared environmental data strategy.
kersti-kaljulaid.locator: Estonia has launched the Data for the Environment Alliance

robert-schuman.example: As French foreign minister, Robert Schuman presented the Schuman Declaration in Paris on 9 May 1950, proposing that Franco-German coal and steel production be placed under a common High Authority within an organisation open to other European countries.
robert-schuman.locator: place their coal and steel production

robert-schuman.example: Representing France as foreign minister, Robert Schuman signed the Statute of the Council of Europe in London on 5 May 1949, joining the new intergovernmental body created to promote cooperation among European states.
robert-schuman.locator: signed the Statute of the Council of Europe

trygve-lie.example: As Minister of Supply and Shipping in the fleeing Norwegian government after the 9 April 1940 German attack, Trygve Lie was central to the government's requisition of the Norwegian commercial fleet, the measure that placed those ships at the Allies' disposal.

Arriving in New York in March 1946 to a UN still housed at the Waldorf Astoria, Trygve Lie had temporary offices provided within weeks and, using his ties to city authorities, saw the organization secure its own Manhattan site before year's end.
trygve-lie.locator: work started at the Waldorf Astoria Hotel

edith-cowan.example: In 1923 Edith Cowan introduced the Women's Legal Status Bill as a Private Member's Bill. It provided that no person be disqualified by sex from public functions, civil or judicial office, or practising law, and it passed.
edith-cowan.locator: from the exercise of any public function

edith-cowan.example: Speaking on her 1923 bill, Edith Cowan pressed for the Women's Legal Status Bill to stand alone, separate from the Interpretations Act, so changes to women's employment status would not require continual amending of that Act.

sukarno.example: At the 1960 General Assembly, Sukarno proposed that newly independent states reshape the UN around anti-colonialism, economic justice, and national sovereignty, urging delegates to adopt these as core principles.
sukarno.locator: the writing of them into the Charter

sukarno.example: In his 1960 General Assembly address, Sukarno identified colonialism, the gap between rich and poor nations, and the forcible division of states as sources of international tension. Indonesia’s delegation returned to that argument at the Assembly two years later.
sukarno.locator: three basic causes of world tension

b-j-habibie.example: In late May 1998, Habibie ordered the Justice Ministry to draft new laws on political parties and elections for the People's Consultative Assembly, and lifted controls on party formation, including the ban on the PRD.
b-j-habibie.locator: draft new laws on political parties and elections

b-j-habibie.example: Within days of taking office in May 1998, Habibie released political prisoners Muchtar Pakpahan and Sri Bintang Pamungkas, and by late August over one hundred others had been freed.

leopold-sedar-senghor.example: In 1966 Senghor presided over the opening in Dakar of the first World Festival of Negro Arts, an event his biography lists among his sustained cultural activities as Senegal's head of state.
leopold-sedar-senghor.locator: à Dakar, le 1 er Festival mondial

leopold-sedar-senghor.example: Elected to the Académie française in 1983, Senghor took seat 16, entering the institution that guards the French language he championed across Africa.
leopold-sedar-senghor.locator: au fauteuil du duc de Lévis-Mirepoix

gough-whitlam.example: In 1953, during his first year in parliament, Whitlam attacked French policies in Indo-China and argued for self-determination for the Vietminh.
On 12 August 1954, Whitlam argued in parliament for recognition of China and its admission to the United Nations.
gough-whitlam.locator: recognition of China and its admission

neville-bonner.example: In 1975 the Senate unanimously adopted a motion by Senator Bonner urging the government to acknowledge prior ownership of Australia by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and to introduce legislation for compensation.
neville-bonner.locator: Original question resolved in the affirmative

neville-bonner.example: In his first Senate speech Bonner objected to the 'blood quanta' rules used to decide who counted as Aboriginal, arguing that anyone who wished to be so classified and had any Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander ancestry should be recognised as Indigenous.
neville-bonner.locator: all persons who desire to be so classified

kamisese-mara.example: In a letter dated 25 November 1980, Fiji's Prime Minister Kamisese Mara replied to New Zealand trade minister Lance Adams-Schneider on orange juice access, continuing the written exchange begun after their October meeting in Suva.
kamisese-mara.locator: Fiji orange juice and the necessary import licences

kamisese-mara.example: Addressing Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser by letter on 6 September 1980, Mara set out Fiji's position within the South Pacific Forum trade negotiation then being conducted through senior officials meeting at Canberra.
kamisese-mara.locator: Concerning Fiji's trading relationship with Australia
